Examples & Exercises

Let f:(0,∞)→(0,∞)f: (0,\infty) \to (0,\infty)f:(0,∞)→(0,∞) satisfy f(1)=1f(1) = 1f(1)=1 and f(x+1)=x f(x)f(x+1) = x\,f(x)f(x+1)=xf(x) for all x>0x > 0x>0. Prove that f(n)=(n−1)!f(n) = (n-1)!f(n)=(n−1)! for every positive integer nnn.

f(1)=1,f(x+1)=x f(x)⟹f(n)=(n−1)!f(1) = 1, \qquad f(x+1) = x\,f(x) \quad \Longrightarrow \quad f(n) = (n-1)!f(1)=1,f(x+1)=xf(x)⟹f(n)=(n−1)!
Show proof
  1. Base case: f(1)=1=0!f(1) = 1 = 0!f(1)=1=0! — given by hypothesis.
  2. Inductive step: assume f(k)=(k−1)!f(k) = (k-1)!f(k)=(k−1)!. Applying the recurrence at x=kx = kx=k gives f(k+1)=k⋅f(k)=k⋅(k−1)!=k!f(k+1) = k \cdot f(k) = k \cdot (k-1)! = k!f(k+1)=k⋅f(k)=k⋅(k−1)!=k!.
  3. By mathematical induction, f(n)=(n−1)!f(n) = (n-1)!f(n)=(n−1)! for every positive integer nnn.
  4. The lesson: this proof uses only the first two conditions — fff is not determined at all between the integers. Indeed the impostor fa(x)=Γ(x)(1+asin⁡2πx)f_a(x) = \Gamma(x)(1 + a\sin 2\pi x)fa​(x)=Γ(x)(1+asin2πx) matches Γ\GammaΓ exactly at every integer nnn (since sin⁡2πn=0\sin 2\pi n = 0sin2πn=0) while differing wildly between them. The third condition (log-convexity) is what closes this gap.

The two limits agree: from In(x)=nn+x UnI_n(x) = \frac{n}{n+x}\,U_nIn​(x)=n+xn​Un​, since nn+x→1\frac{n}{n+x} \to 1n+xn​→1 and Un→G(x)U_n \to G(x)Un​→G(x) (squeeze), In(x)→G(x)I_n(x) \to G(x)In​(x)→G(x); but also In(x)→Γ(x)I_n(x) \to \Gamma(x)In​(x)→Γ(x).
